acceptance: --datagen-backend native generates TPC-DS at SF 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 through the library, SHA-256 identical to patched dsdgen.
The native TPC-H maintenance path takes RF1/RF2 from library write_refresh, byte-identical to dbgen -U at SF 0.01 and 1; a test runs it with dbgen absent.
Native TPC-DS maintenance fails loudly ('TPC-DS refresh sets are not native yet') until datagen-bb-tpcds-refresh-wiring lands.
PR CI runs TPC-DS parity at SF 0.01, 0.1 and 1.0 (24 tables, SHA-256 and bidirectional EXCEPT ALL on Parquet).
A required check on benchbox-datagen pin changes runs TPC-H and TPC-DS parity at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 plus result_digest.py.
description:
## Problem
datagen-lib-benchbox-integration covers TPC-H and TPC-DS at SF >= 1. Nothing routes TPC-DS below SF 1 or TPC-H RF1/RF2 (both TPC cutover prerequisites) through the library, and the ADR's TPC-DS PR check and library-version-bump check have no owner.

## Change
Wire native TPC-DS at fractional scales and the TPC-H maintenance path (library write_refresh); add the TPC-DS PR parity check and a required check on library pin changes.

## Decision gates
- If a fractional scale accepted by BenchBox (TPCDS_MIN_SUBSCALE and the registry rules) is not covered by library parity evidence, stop and report rather than widening the accepted set.
- SF 10 parity in the pin-bump check runs under the heavy lock or on CI runners only.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree; heavy work only through make heavy-run; never kill processes by name pattern.
- No divergent fork of tpcgen-rs; carried patches only under the 2026-11-27 rule (<= ~200 changed lines, upstream PR, SHA pin, README entry); anything larger goes to the owner with sizes first.
- Human commit identity, no agent attribution. Report only observed results.
